NO. 048 · The Kingfishers / Alcedinidae · Kingfishers

White-throated Kingfisher

白胸翡翠 · bái xiōng fěi cuì Halcyon smyrnensis
Resident Common 27–29 cm Protected (Class II) IUCN LC

Chestnut head, snow-white breast, a big red bill

Much larger than a Common Kingfisher and far more heavily coloured: head and neck chestnut, breast and belly snow-white, back and wings deep brilliant blue, and a big scarlet bill. It has little need of water, and often sits on a wire waiting for lizards and insects.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • HeadHead, neck and sides of the underparts chestnut; throat and centre of the breast pure white, making a broad white bib.
  • Back & wingsBack, wings and tail brilliant blue to blue-green with a strong metallic sheen — in flight, a streak of blue light.
  • BillBright red, heavy and long — one of the most conspicuous features of the species.
  • SizeAbout 28 cm long, plainly larger than Common Kingfisher, thick-set, with a relatively short tail.

Behaviour

Its diet is broader than a Common Kingfisher's: besides fish and prawns it takes quantities of insects, lizards, frogs and even small mice, which is why it is often found in farmland, grassland and scrub far from water. It hunts from wires, dead branches and rooftops, dropping onto the ground after prey. A nationally protected species (Class II). It tunnels into earth banks and embankments to nest.

Voice

A loud, harsh 'kilili—kilili', a descending series of whistles, given in flight or from a perch — an easy sound to notice in open country.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen farmland
  • Qi'ao village edges
  • Jinwan grassy slopes
  • Tangjiawan
Field note
A nationally protected species (Class II). Separating it from Common Kingfisher: much larger, a broad white breast, a red bill, and it often hunts well away from water.
